references.text: Hanging or displaying lawbreakers as a means to appease the Lord's wrath, a similar punishment method mentioned in the Mosaic Law
Joshua hung the king of Ai on a tree until sunset, the same practice of hanging 'for the Lord' as a public punishment
The five kings were hung on trees until sunset, showing the same practice of public execution
Saul's descendants were hung for the Lord in Gibea to turn away the Lord's wrath, a direct parallel to the incident at Peor
Phinehas' action turned away the Lord's burning wrath from Israel, fulfilling what was commanded in verse 4
The context of the Lord's wrath: Israel's sin with Baal-Peor that led to this judgment
A similar situation where leaders had to carry out judgment to stop the Lord's wrath after the golden calf sin
Reference back to the Baal-Peor incident and how the Lord destroyed those who followed Baal
The psalmist's retelling of the Baal-Peor incident and Phinehas' intervention that stopped the plague
